story.speaker: Gigabyte
story.message: Welcome to my workshop! Every game runs on a game loop — update, draw, repeat.

story.speaker: Gigabyte
story.message: Update moves things, draw shows them on screen, and it all repeats dozens of times per second.

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: That's why characters in games move so smoothly!

concept.title: The game loop
concept.explanation: A game loop repeats three steps very fast: read input, update the game world, then draw it on screen.

playground.instructions: Arrange the three steps of a game loop in the order they should run.

challenge.prompt: Put the game loop steps in the correct order.

story.speaker: Gigabyte
story.message: A sprite is the picture for a game character or object.

story.speaker: Gigabyte
story.message: Every sprite has an x and y position — x is left/right, y is up/down.

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: Move x up and the sprite slides right!

concept.title: Sprites & coordinates
concept.explanation: A sprite's position is described with two numbers: x (horizontal) and y (vertical). Increasing x moves it right; increasing y moves it down.

playground.instructions: Drag the sprite and watch its x and y values change.

challenge.prompt: To move a sprite further to the right, you should:

story.speaker: Gigabyte
story.message: How does a game know when two things bump into each other? Collision detection!

story.speaker: Gigabyte
story.message: The simplest check: are two sprites overlapping in both x and y?

story.speaker: Pixel
story.message: That's how coins get collected and obstacles get hit.

concept.title: Collision detection
concept.explanation: Two sprites collide when their positions overlap. Games check this every frame to trigger events like collecting a coin.

playground.instructions: Drag the hero sprite toward the coin and see when the collision message appears.

challenge.prompt: Fill in the blank to check if the hero touches a coin.
